correctness.rationale: Exact derivative, cubic discriminants and branch discriminant resultant give disjoint index-two branch sets for p>=11, with common index-three branch t=0. The two connected degree-three covers have geometric S3 monodromy and independent quadratic Galois quotients, implying regular S3 x S3 splitting group. Riemann-Hurwitz yields g=13; a three-cycle Frobenius twist gives nine points per irreducible pair and at most 93 exceptional rational points. Weil then gives |9Np-(p+1)|<=26sqrt(p)+93 and positivity p>=851. A complete certified exact prime-by-prime sieve through 850 verifies the remaining 146 primes, finding exactly {2,3,5,13}. Finite checking is not substituted for an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general S3 x S3 specialization theorems imply the first-order p/9 asymptotic once geometric monodromy is supplied. They do not provide the exact genus, explicit error constant or exhaustive list of primes for this rigid paired family. Pan treats a distinct quadratic/cubic pair.

originality.rationale: The strongest relevant general result already proves p/9+O(sqrt p) from S3 x S3 geometric monodromy and this is credited. The independently specific parts are genus thirteen, a numerical 26 sqrt(p)+93 deviation bound, an effective 851 cutoff and the complete all-prime exclusion set {2,3,5,13}. Jones considers monogenicity of the underlying integer family; Pan addresses a different quadratic/cubic pair; the closest published simultaneous-cubic result is characteristic three and not this pair. No known inspected statement implies the exact classification; earlier implicit coverage remains a real risk.
residual_risks: An earlier paper might derive the exact sign-pair classification as an unstated corollary of parameterized cubic factorization.
The 2012 Harrington paper and the most similar published short abstract were not read completely; their inspected accessible material does not imply this prime-field classification.
A database search and the current selection of primary literature cannot guarantee uniqueness.

value.rationale: The naturally sign-paired cubic specializations are part of a studied geometric-series family. Their joint finite-field irreducibility is an arithmetic condition not captured by a separate monogenicity criterion. A sharp all-prime existence classification, effective uniform bound and explicit genus-thirteen mechanism give a motivated and complete solution rather than an arbitrary finite slice or unquantified special-case asymptotic.
